memory_candidates.content: When wrapping an untracked, self-updating vendor terminal CLI with a pty-proxy to add output styling, keep the byte-chunk filter free of real-time buffering except for the ONE marker that genuinely requires look-ahead (e.g. a fixed-grammar prompt string with no trailing newline). Everything else -- a handoff-line marker, a transient status-indicator toggle -- can be detected via small bounded rolling windows that never withhold output, so long streamed content (e.g. a chat answer) is never delayed waiting on a match decision. Also: readline/canonical-mode redraws always return to column 0 via \r, never \n, so 'arrived via \n' vs 'arrived via \r' is a reliable, cheap discriminator for 'fresh occurrence' vs 'redraw re-emission' of the same marker text -- structurally disqualify \r-arrivals from matching rather than adding a separate suppression flag.

When testing a pty-harness subprocess via Python's subprocess.Popen with stdin=PIPE: closing the test's own stdin pipe (as communicate() does) only stops forwarding into the child's pty -- it does NOT deliver EOF to the child's still-open pty slave, exactly like a real terminal. A stub child that calls input() a second time after that will hang forever. Design the stub to exit without waiting on a second read, rather than chasing an EOF-propagation mechanism that would not reflect real interactive usage anyway. Also: always capture the forked grandchild's PID (not just the immediate Popen child) when debugging a hang, since proc.kill() only kills the immediate child and leaves the pty's own forked subprocess orphaned.

lazy.nvim's VeryLazy event does not fire within a short `nvim --headless -c '...' -c 'qa'` sequence, so a plan verification bullet that runs `:SomeCommand` to check a lazy-loaded plugin's command registration will spuriously fail headless (confirmed as a pre-existing, environment-level timing gap, not a regression) -- and if the command happens to start a real subprocess (e.g. a network-backed CLI), running it for real can hang and leave orphaned processes behind a forced kill. Substitute: `dofile()` the plugin spec directly, call its `config()` function with `pcall`, then check `vim.api.nvim_get_commands({})` for the expected command name -- this exercises the same `nvim_create_user_command` call without depending on lazy.nvim's load timing and without executing the command for real.
